title: DevSecOps Lead- London
descriptionHtml:
About Hiya

At Hiya, we’re making business calls more trusted, useful, and effective.

Voice remains one of the most important ways businesses communicate with their customers, but the value of a call depends on trust. When customers do not recognize who is calling or why, important conversations are missed, customer relationships suffer, and business outcomes are harder to achieve.

Hiya helps businesses create trusted calling experiences that benefit both sides of the conversation: enterprises can reach customers with confidence, and customers can answer with confidence. Our products support branded business calling, trusted caller identity, call performance insights, customer engagement, and voice security capabilities that help businesses strengthen relationships and improve outcomes.

This role sits in a core business area for Hiya and is focused on helping SMB and enterprise customers succeed.

About the Position

The Lead DevSecOps Engineer is a leadership and individual contributor role responsible for maturing our security posture across all engineering departments. You will lead the design and implementation of automated, platform-based security solutions, enabling teams to build secure software while maintaining velocity. You will partner closely with Core Tech, Product, and Engineering leadership to define our security roadmap and culture.

We’re excited about you because you are a trailblazer who balances high-level strategy with hands-on technical execution. You are comfortable building from near-scratch, thrive on educating others, and possess a "platform" mindset that prioritizes empowering developers over acting as a gatekeeper.

What You’ll Do

  • Define and execute a multi-quarter security roadmap for the entire engineering organization.

  • Develop and maintain platform-level security tools that enable automated, self-service security for feature teams.

  • Partner with Core Tech to integrate security primitives into our standard CI/CD and cloud deployment workflows.

  • Conduct cross-team discovery to assess current security posture and identify high-risk technical debt.

  • Mentor junior and peer engineers, fostering a culture where security is integrated into the "you build it, you run it" philosophy.

  • Stay ahead of evolving threat landscapes, specifically regarding supply chain risks and large-scale AI infrastructure.

  • Own and mature our existing detection, SIEM, and incident-response tooling as part of building out the broader security platform — this role inherits live systems, it isn't a blank canvas.

  • Act as a security collaborator to IT on AI-usage risk (data exposure via connectors/agents, prompt injection) — distinct from, and in addition to, securing the AI systems Hiya builds as a product.

Qualities that will make you successful:

  • Deep understanding of cloud-native architecture (AWS) and modern security best practices.

  • Proven experience designing "self-service" platforms that developers actually want to use.

  • Strong communication skills—the ability to turn complex security concerns into decisions engineers and stakeholders can act on.

  • High proficiency in at least one modern language and familiarity with agent-based/AI-assisted development tools.

  • Pragmatism—knowing when to accept calculated tech debt in favor of high-impact outcomes.

  • A leadership style rooted in empathy, collaborative debate, and commitment to team decisions.

  • Builds systems, documentation, and team capability that outlast you — we're wary of highly productive engineers who leave behind bespoke, unmaintainable tooling that has to be scrapped when they move on.

The person in this role must embody Hiya’s key values of Serving our customers, Doing rather than observing, Improving ourselves and our business, Owning and holding ourselves accountable for success, and Leading by showing up with a point of view, engaging in open discussion, listening respectfully to others opinions and committing to decisions.

The requirements listed in the job descriptions are guidelines. You don’t have to satisfy every requirement or meet every qualification listed. If your skills are transferable we would still love to hear from you.

How We Work

Hiya is not a passive environment. We expect people to take ownership, form opinions, and engage directly with hard problems.

We work with a high degree of transparency and autonomy. Context is shared openly, and decisions are discussed, challenged, and then made. Once a call is made, we commit and move forward.

You'll be expected to work through ambiguity, weigh tradeoffs, and take responsibility for results, while keeping a high bar for quality and customer trust.

Every team member at Hiya is expected to live our core values:

  • Serve, our customers and partners by holding a high bar for trust and quality

  • Own, share in success and open up to failures

  • Lead, listen, show up with a point of view but commit entirely once a decision has been made

  • Improve, even if it means changing course or contradicting ourselves

  • Do, rather than observe

How We Invest in You

Compensation & Ownership
Equity Compensation: ownership aligned with your impact and the company's growth

We offer an L&D budget to support your growth and real internal mobility so career pathing isn't just a talking point — because we're building this with people who own the outcome.

 

Come Work With Us!

We're building a team with diverse perspectives, identities, and professional experiences. We evaluate candidates through a business lens and believe that diversity and unique viewpoints make our company stronger, more dynamic, and a great place to build a career.

We've been recognized by Built In, GeekWire, Comparably, G2, Forbes, and Deloitte Technology Fast 500 for our culture, innovation, leadership, compensation, and more. At Hiya, we're a people-centric company focused on helping each employee grow both personally and professionally. We create a culture of support and empowerment that challenges the status quo, resulting in an energized team that's passionate about their work. You'll love working here if you're looking for an innovative challenge that's disrupting an industry. Come join us!

Hiya is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to building an inclusive environment for all employees.

Compensation: £80K – £120K • Offers Equity

title: Director, Development Cost Management & Capital Planning EMEA
descriptionHtml:
Director, Development Cost & Capital Planning (EMEA) 

Location: London, hybrid, with regular travel to project locations across EMEA

About Nscale

At Nscale, we are building the infrastructure for Europe’s AI revolution. Nscale is developing cutting-edge sovereign generative AI solutions, powered by a new generation of high-performance, sustainable data centres and GPUs built specifically for AI workloads. 

The growth of artificial intelligence is driving unprecedented global demand for compute and GPU infrastructure. Nscale is positioned at the heart of this transformation — building the platforms that will enable the next decade of innovation. 

Nscale is working closely with the world’s most advanced AI technology providers, integrating next-gen compute hardware and GPU clusters in both partner and Nscale built facilities. This is a unique opportunity to join Nscale’s journey, play a key role in delivering transformative AI infrastructure, and help shape a company scaling globally with a key focus in the EMEA region.

The Role

The Director, Development Cost & Capital Planning is accountable for establishing cost certainty, capital planning, development risk and commercial viability across Nscale's EMEA Development portfolio from site identification (Gate 0) through due diligence (Gate 1) to development sanction and ‘shovel-ready’ transition into Delivery (Gate 2).

The role owns L0 Indicative Estimates, L1 Estimated Budgets and L2 Schematic Design Budget for every EMEA opportunity, consolidating the development, energy, design, construction, procurement and AI infrastructure workstream budgets into a single Total Development Cost (TDC) providing the commercial and financial foundation for site selection, land and lease acquisitions, Colocation leases, underwriting business cases, investment committee approvals and project approvals.

Operating as an individual contributor at first, the role will personally prepare estimates, cost models, risk registers, benchmarking and investment-grade business cases while establishing the systems, governance and processes required for future growth. The role will develop to manage a high performing team supporting the Development function as it expands across the EMEA region.

Key Responsibilities

Who You Are

Preferred:

title: Director of Compliance and Risk (UK)
descriptionHtml:
About BJAK

BJAK is Southeast Asia’s largest digital insurance platform, expanding financial access through automation, data, and digital scale. As we grow across markets, we are committed to building a platform that is safe, compliant, and trusted.

We are hiring a Director of Compliance and Risk (UK) to lead regulatory strategy, risk governance, and compliance operations for our UK market entry and expansion alongside the CEO. This role is expected to hold the SMF16 (Compliance Oversight) Senior Management Function once approved, and will act as our primary point of contact with the FCA.

This is a build role: you'll be creating frameworks, policies, and controls from scratch rather than inheriting an existing function.

 

Why This Role Matters

The Director of Compliance and Risk (UK) will:

  • Design and enforce compliance frameworks that enable safe scaling of digital financial services.

  • Ensure BJAK operates in accordance with UK regulatory standards, especially FCA requirements.

  • Protect consumers through transparent, fair, and ethical practices.

  • Establish BJAK as a trusted partner with regulators, partners, and industry stakeholders.

  • Build compliance capability and culture across the company.

 

What You Will Do

Regulatory Leadership & Strategy

  • Develop and maintain compliance frameworks aligned with UK regulatory requirements.

  • Lead regulatory readiness for market entry, licensing, and ongoing supervision.

  • Serve as the primary contact with the FCA and relevant UK bodies.

  • Interpret regulatory changes and guide business strategy accordingly.

 

Risk Governance & Compliance Operations

  • Build policies and controls covering AML, KYC, data privacy, consumer duty, distribution, and claims-related compliance.

  • Conduct risk assessments and implement remediation plans for identified gaps.

  • Establish monitoring, testing, and reporting processes for ongoing compliance.

  • Ensure internal audits, compliance reviews, and control testing are operationalised.

 

Consumer Protection & Business Integrity

  • Embed fairness, transparency, and responsible selling throughout the organisation.

  • Oversee product compliance, marketing reviews, pricing governance, and distribution oversight.

  • Implement complaint handling frameworks aligned with regulatory standards.

 

Cross-Functional Support & Training

  • Partner with product, operations, legal, marketing, and commercial teams to ensure compliant execution.

  • Provide guidance on regulatory implications of new products, partnerships, or distribution models.

  • Deliver training to ensure teams understand and execute compliance responsibilities.

 

You Will Thrive in This Role If You

  • See compliance as a strategic enabler, not a blocker.

  • Operate with high integrity, sound judgment, and strong attention to detail.

  • Communicate clearly and influence leaders using data and logic.

  • Enjoy building frameworks and scaling systems from early-stage to mature environments.

  • Thrive in fast-paced, evolving settings where regulation meets innovation.

 

What You Bring

  • 8+ years of compliance, risk, or regulatory experience within financial services, insurance, insurtech, or fintech.

  • Deep understanding of UK regulatory frameworks, including FCA rules and consumer duty requirements.

  • Experience in compliance for digital platforms, distribution, or insurance products (preferred).

  • Proven ability to design policies, conduct risk assessments, and manage complex compliance programs.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including dealing with regulators.

 

Bonus (Nice to Have)

  • Experience in start-up or high-growth environments.

  • Previous SMF experience.

  • Background in insurtech, digital distribution, or online marketplaces.

  • Knowledge of GDPR, AML, sanctions, or cross-border compliance.

 

Location Requirement

  • This role is based in the UK. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our London office at least 3 days per week.

 

Why Join Us

  • Shape compliance for a fast-growing international fintech-insurtech platform.

  • Build frameworks that enable safe, inclusive financial access at scale.

  • Work closely with leadership and regulators to drive responsible innovation.

  • Competitive compensation with long-term growth and international career opportunities.


Compensations Range

  • We offer a highly competitive package, ranging from £100,000 to £150,000, reflecting both experience and suitability for this pivotal role.

title: Director of Engineering, Communications
descriptionHtml:
The Communications Tribe

The Communications Tribe is part of HelloFresh's Growth Alliance. Our mission is to enable a highly personalised, automated CRM communication ecosystem that prioritises user-centric engagement across our owned channels: email, push, SMS, in-app and embedded.

The problems we are solving:

  • How anyone with a good reason to speak to customers can do it safely and in minutes.
  • How we make sure every customer gets the right message, at the right moment, through the right channel, so that our communication is truly personal.
  • How we move to an autonomous, self-optimising system that continuously learns from every past interaction and gets better with each send.
  • How we make sure we can reach our customers in their preferred channels.

Our vision is to decentralise how HelloFresh talks to people across the whole relationship with us: prospects, subscribers and those who have left. Setting up and steering communications stops being the job of a small group of specialists and becomes something teams across the business can do safely, on top of tools and an intelligence layer that we build and that learn from every send. That loop reaches beyond CRM, so the customer experience is coherent from the first ad someone sees to the communication that converts and retains them.

As Director of Engineering, Communications, you will lead the engineering organisation that makes this real. You will set technical direction, hold the bar for reliability and operational excellence, and partner with Product, Marketing and CRM teams to turn the vision into working systems.

descriptionHtml:

Our delivery model is shifting from large time-and-materials teams to small, AI-first pods working against a business outcome. As Market Lead, you will shape how we take that model to UKI clients: what we sell, how we price it, and how we staff and deliver it. You will lead a core team of 5–6 direct reports and a wider matrix of around 50-75 people across UKI, and you will help them build the skills this shift requires. We are developing these ways of working together.

Job qualifications

Technical Skills

  • P&L & Operations Ownership: Hard business acumen required to manage £50–£75M TCV and £45–£50M ACV, including driving margins, utilization, bench management, and capacity planning.

Professional Skills

  • Suite Advisory & Presence: Exceptional ability to act as a strategic sparring partner to CDOs, CIOs, and CFOs. Comfort challenging client assumptions and negotiating ROI and business cases at the executive level.

  • Navigating Ambiguity: High resilience and drive. The ability to build momentum and define strategy while internal delivery models, pricing structures, and competency frameworks are still maturing.

  • Coaching & Capability Building: A strong mentoring mindset focused on reskilling existing talent, raising the overall AI fluency of the practice, and shifting the team towards AI-first delivery pods.

At Lucis, AI isn't just our product, it's our engine. 100% of our teams are equipped with the best AI agents. You have carte blanche to explore and automate everything that can be, so you can focus exclusively on high-value work.

title: Embedded Staff Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Embedded Staff Engineer - Help us build the Control System that the world can rely on. 

About Priva  

Your Future Ecosystem  

Located between Rotterdam and The Hague, in the heart of the world’s leading greenhouse region, lies Westland, home to Priva’s modern campus in De Lier. This innovative region has been the foundation of our family-owned company since the 1950s.  

What started as a hardware business has grown into a global leader in horticulture and building automation. Today, Priva develops advanced hardware, software, and digital services for climate control, energy efficiency, and water optimization. Our solutions support horticulture, indoor and city farming, as well as offices, hotels, hospitals, and retail environments worldwide.  

Our next ambition? Becoming a leading digital service provider with “Climate as a Service” solutions that help customers operate more sustainably.  

With over 600 colleagues, 16 international offices, and more than 400 installation partners, we deliver smart, sustainable solutions in over 100 countries. 

If you want your work to have impact on sustainability, food security, and the way cities grow, then this is where you belong.    
 

Why this role matters

At Priva, we are building the next generation of IoT-enabled building automation systems: cloud-connected, security-first, and designed for long-term reliability. As a Embedded Staff Engineer (C++ / Linux), you will play a key role in shaping a scalable platform that combines embedded controllers, edge gateways, and cloud services. Your work ensures that buildings operate safely, efficiently, and reliably for 10-15 years with minimal maintenance. This role goes beyond implementation. You will drive technical direction, influence software architecture, and support complex system design decisions across our platform.

Your role as Staff Engineer

You act as the bridge between software architecture and implementation, guiding teams in building a service-oriented, event-driven IoT platform consisting of 15+ services running on embedded devices. You bring deep expertise in modern C++ (10+) and embedded Linux, and you help ensure scalability, reliability, and maintainability across the system.

Your team

You will join our Prime team, a group of highly experienced embedded software engineers and test engineers, working on cutting-edge building automation technology.

What you’ll do

  • Design and develop embedded software in modern C++ (C++17 or later) on Linux 

  • Build scalable, modular, and configurable control components 

  • Implement deterministic and real-time control strategies 

  • Develop robust 24/7 runtime systems for real-world environments 

  • Create simulation environments and automated test frameworks 

  • Lead technical design principles for embedded teams and align with our embedded architects on fit within overall architecture

  • Ensure quality solutions by leading the definition and adherence to technical design and coding guidelines

  • Promote craftmanship, quality gates and responsible AI practices across our embedded engineering community

  • Support application lifecycle management (ALM) 

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (hardware, cloud, QA) 


What you bring

  • 10+ years of experience in Embedded Software Engineering (C++ / Linux) 

  • Strong expertise in modern C++ (C++17 or later) 

  • Solid understanding of software architecture, design patterns, and SOLID principles 

  • Experience with multi threading, concurrency, and performance optimization 

  • Experience with distributed or service-oriented systems 

  • Knowledge of communication protocols such as MQTT, CAN, Serial 

  • Experience working in resource-constrained environments (real-time systems) 

  • Ability to review, challenge, and improve architectural decisions 

  • Strong debugging and system-level problem-solving skills 

  • Experience working in cross-functional and international teams

Nice to have

  • Experience in IoT, building automation, or industrial systems 

  • Familiarity with (industrial) control systems

  • Experience with Yocto, Docker, or containerized environments 

  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines and DevOps practices 

  • Experience with test strategies, automated testing, and system validation

What you get  
In numbers 

  • A competitive salary based on your experience; 

  • We find a healthy work-life balance important: working flexible hours combined with 30 vacation days a year and the option to buy more; 

  • 8% holiday allowance; 

  • Travel allowance of € 0,23/km with a daily maximum of 150 kilometers. 

For your own sustainability 

  • Be secured with our pension plan; 

  • Feel engaged and join our participation plan; 

  • Keep on learning with your personal education possibilities and budget; 

  • Be happy and fit by using our healthy cafeteria, our free on-premises fitness where you can participate in CrossFit, Pilates and Spinning classes or play table tennis or table football.

Our values 
Priva's mission is to create an optimal environment where people can work, grow and develop. We offer worldwide solutions for horticulture and building automation. Our ambition is to be known as the leading technology and service provider for sustainable urban deltas. We are proud that our solutions result in lower consumption of natural resources and contribute to some of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). 
 
Our culture is built around our core values; sustainable, innovation, make it happen and human. In our latest employment survey, our colleagues mainly described our culture as: open, ambitious, innovative, friendly, committed, informal, flexible and down to earth. We aim to be a dynamic, fast-paced, flat and informal organization, where our colleagues have the space to grow and develop. 
 
We believe that to be successful, it is important to include people with different perspectives, backgrounds and cultures. Every day, we continue to build our open culture with people who are driven to turn our vision into reality, regardless of who they love, where they are from, or what they believe in. We encourage and celebrate people to voice their opinions and be their authentic selves.

title: EMEA Sales Lead
descriptionHtml:
About Firstwork

Labour markets are broken. Millions of people are ready to work and can't start. Screening, right-to-work checks, contracts, onboarding and scheduling still run across disconnected systems, with hundreds of manual decisions in between. Firstwork builds AI agents that run frontline workforce operations end to end. We activate hundreds of thousands of workers a month globally for some of the world's largest employers and staffing firms, working forward-deployed inside the customer's operation. Backed by Y Combinator and Gradient (Google’s AI fund), with offices in New York, with London and Dubai opening later this year.

Why this role

European customers are not evaluating us out of curiosity. Workforce compliance has turned into a board-level risk and there are deadlines attached to it. The demand is already here. What we don't have is coverage, or an enterprise motion that repeats.

You are the first commercial hire in Europe and you build the team around you. It is a player-coach role and it stays that way, because we are not going to put someone in charge of coaching a European motion; they have never run against European buyers themselves. You carry a quota while you hire. A Solutions Consultant joins alongside you, SDRs come after that, and how the pod fits together is your call.

None of this starts from zero. The North American playbook holds up on qualification, pricing, security review and technical validation. Your job is to work out which parts of it survive European procurement, works councils and regulators, rebuild the rest, and turn the result into the thing every rep in the region runs.

  • Build and qualify pipeline in staffing, healthcare, logistics, manufacturing and retail

  • Turn the North American motion into a European playbook other people can run

  • Seven or more years selling complex enterprise software, with six and seven figure closes you can talk us through in detail

  • Time selling into staffing, healthcare, logistics, manufacturing and/or retail

descriptionHtml:
🏗️ À propos de Bricks

Chez Bricks, on construit la façon la plus simple d’investir dans l’immobilier, à partir de 10 €. Aujourd’hui, plus de 670 000 membres utilisent notre plateforme.

Quelques jalons : passage chez Capital (M6) en 2022, Tony Parker investisseur et ambassadeur, record européen de vitesse de levée avec 5 M€ collectés en 5 secondes, puis plus de 20 M€ en 10 jours auprès de notre communauté.

En 2025, Bricks a collecté 176 M€, soit +90 % en un an, tout en atteignant la rentabilité.

Derrière cette croissance, il y a un produit B2C régulé, des flux financiers réels, des enjeux forts de sécurité, de fiabilité et de cohérence des données. Ce qui part en production peut être utilisé par des milliers d’investisseurs dans les heures qui suivent.

Côté Engineering, on fonctionne avec une équipe autonome, proche du produit et du business. On attend de chacun qu’il comprenne les problèmes en profondeur, prenne des décisions et contribue directement à la qualité de ce qu’on construit.

Vos missions

🧩 Le job

Tu rejoindras une équipe Engineering de 10 ingénieurs, avec un CTO qui code au quotidien. Côté Produit : 2 Designers et 2 PM.

L’équipe grandit, les enjeux aussi. On cherche aujourd’hui un Engineering Manager qui travaillera étroitement avec le CTO, à la fois sur le management de l’équipe, son organisation et les sujets techniques structurants.

Tu participeras aux roadmaps Engineering, à la composition des squads, à la définition des objectifs et aux prochains recrutements, tout en restant proche du code et du produit.

Chez Bricks, devenir manager ne veut pas dire s’éloigner de la technique : tu dois pouvoir entrer dans une discussion d’architecture, challenger une décision, faire une code review utile ou débloquer un sujet complexe.

🧱 Ce que tu vas owner

👉 Construire l’organisation Engineering avec le CTO : faire évoluer la composition des équipes, les objectifs, les façons de travailler et participer activement aux recrutements.

👉 Manager et faire progresser les ingénieurs au quotidien : 1:1, feedback, accompagnement, progression, exigence technique. Comprendre ce qui bloque quelqu’un et l’aider à passer au palier suivant.

👉 Rester connecté au code et au produit. Tu ne coderas pas nécessairement toute la journée, mais tu dois pouvoir entrer dans la codebase, participer aux reviews et prendre part aux décisions d’architecture.

👉 Créer les conditions pour que l’équipe shippe vite et bien. Identifier les blocages, arbitrer, clarifier les responsabilités et faire évoluer le process uniquement lorsqu’il apporte de la valeur.

👉 Maintenir un haut niveau d’exigence technique. Modélisation du domaine, architecture, qualité des données, sécurité, performance : tu aides l’équipe à prendre les bonnes décisions là où elles comptent vraiment.

🛠️ La stack

Tu dois être suffisamment proche de notre environnement technique pour pouvoir intervenir réellement dans les discussions et dans le code :

👉 TypeScript end-to-end. Les types sont de la documentation qui s’exécute.

👉 Node monolithe, Screaming Architecture.

👉 Postgres (NeonDB) avec Graphile pour les queues ACID. Redis pour ce qui doit être rapide.

👉 Zod, Kysely, ts-pattern - type-safety du front à la DB.

👉 Better Auth.

👉 Railway pour l’infra.

👉 Github CI, Datadog, K6.

👉 React Native + RN Web côté front : une seul codebase web + mobile.

Tu n’as pas besoin d’avoir utilisé exactement chacune de ces technos. En revanche, Node/TypeScript et une vraie profondeur backend sont importants : on cherche quelqu’un capable de challenger techniquement l’équipe, pas seulement de la manager.

🤖 IA-first mindset

L’IA est partout dans notre quotidien. 100**% des workflows passe par elle** : Claude Code, Claude Cowork, Cursor, Automations, etc.

Et pour un Engineering Manager, l’enjeu va plus loin que sa propre utilisation : tu dois comprendre comment l’IA transforme la façon de manager, coder, de reviewer, de tester, de recruter et de faire progresser une équipe Engineering.

Si tu vois encore l’IA comme secondaire, ce poste n’est pas pour toi.

Vos compétences

🎯 Tu fitteras si...

👉 Tu as d’abord été Senior Software Engineer et tu n’as pas quitté la technique en devenant manager. Tu aimes toujours le code, tu restes proche des sujets techniques et tu peux encore mettre les mains dedans quand c’est nécessaire.

👉 Tu sais construire et faire vivre une équipe Engineering. Recruter, intégrer, faire progresser, donner du feedback et faire évoluer les responsabilités font partie du rôle.

👉 Tu as une forte expérience backend Node /TypeScript en environnement produit.

👉 Tu sais prendre de la hauteur. Au-delà du management individuel, tu réfléchis à la composition des équipes, aux responsabilités, aux recrutements et à la façon dont l’organisation doit évoluer.

👉 Tu sais quand ralentir et quand shipper. Tout ne mérite pas 3 semaines de réflexion, mais tout ne mérite pas non plus un quick fix.

👉 Tu es pragmatique et tu préfères construire une organisation adaptée au contexte plutôt qu’appliquer un playbook tout fait.

👉 Tu reconnais tes erreurs sans en faire un drame. Tu peux changer d’avis quand quelqu’un apporte de meilleurs arguments.

👉 La fintech, l’investissement ou l’immobilier t’intéresse : gros bonus si tu investis toi-même.

❌ Tu ne fitteras pas si...

👉 Tu veux sortir de la technique en devenant manager.

👉 Tu cherches un rôle principalement centré sur le delivery, les cérémonies et le suivi de process.

👉 Tu veux appliquer un modèle d’organisation tout fait, sans l’adapter au contexte.

👉 Tu as besoin d’une séparation nette entre management, technique et produit.

👉 Tu veux être le point de passage de toutes les décisions techniques. Ici, ton rôle est aussi de faire grandir des ingénieurs autonomes, pas de décider à leur place.

Avantages

L'offre

👉 CDI, temps plein.

👉 Un produit B2C utilisé par 700 000+ membres, ce que ton équipe construit a un impact concret et immédiat.

👉 Un rôle au cœur de l’organisation Engineering : tu travailleras directement avec le CTO et auras un impact réel sur la façon dont l’équipe se structure et évolue.

👉 Une boîte ambitieuse, rentable et en forte croissance

👉 Salaire compétitif, MacBook Pro de ton choix, tout le matériel qu’il te faut.

👉 Hybride Montpellier : office-first (2j/sem de remote) ou remote-first (~2j/mois au bureau).

Déroulement des entretiens

  1. Pré-qualification téléphonique avec notre recruteuse

  2. Echange manager avec Denis, notre CTO (1h)

  3. Entretien technique : cadrage technique et implémentation d'une fonctionnalité

  4. Entretien team-fit (1h)

  5. Rencontre avec Cédric, notre fondateur (45 min)

  6. Offre

descriptionHtml:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Engineering Teams

Wayve is building embodied AI that can drive any vehicle, anywhere. Within Robot Software, the Platform Integration team brings together the software and interfaces that enable our AI Driver to operate on new development platforms.

The team owns early vehicle software integration, drive-by-wire and the vehicle facing software drivers. We work across software, hardware, controls and operations to bring up new vehicle variants, improve their reliability and establish repeatable processes for validation and handover.

As Engineering Manager, you’ll lead the engineers responsible for this work, shaping both the team’s technical direction and its development. Your team will help Wayve scale across vehicles and OEM programmes by building reusable software interfaces and making integration more predictable.

🧠 Your day-to-day

You’ll be accountable for the team’s delivery, engagement, resourcing, roadmap and performance. You’ll coach engineers, support their career development, lead hiring and build a team with clear ownership and high standards.

Working with the team, you’ll set direction across vehicle interfacing software and integration practices. You’ll help the team balance immediate programme needs with longer-term investments in architecture, tooling and reliability.

You’ll also coordinate dependencies across teams, make priorities and trade-offs clear, and resolve risks early. The role combines software engineering leadership with practical delivery and execution.

🧩 What you’ll be working on:

Leading and developing engineers: Set clear expectations, run effective one-to-ones, provide regular feedback, manage performance and support career progression.

Building the team: Own hiring and onboarding, develop the skills needed for future programmes and build a collaborative culture across locations.

Setting direction and priorities: Maintain the team’s mission, ownership boundaries and roadmap, balancing programme commitments with improvements that make future integrations easier.

Delivering new vehicle integrations: Lead planning and execution from early preparation and bench integration through vehicle bring-up, validation and handover. Secure the resources and cross-team support needed for delivery.

Owning vehicle-facing software: Guide the architecture and development of Vehicle Driver and drive-by-wire components, building robust interfaces that reduce bespoke changes for each vehicle variant.

Improving reliability and release quality: Establish measurable reliability targets, use field feedback to prioritise improvements, and build strong ownership of testing, releases and escalated issues. Invest in sustainable over the air updatable infrastructure.

Making integration repeatable: Develop playbooks, tooling, runbooks and knowledge-transfer practices so subsequent vehicles can be commissioned and supported independently.

Driving technical collaboration: Review designs and work closely with software, hardware, controls, safety and operations teams, as well as customers and suppliers where needed, to resolve integration challenges.

🙌 You should apply if:

You have a strong track record of leading and developing software or systems engineering teams, including coaching, hiring, performance management and career development.

You have owned a team roadmap and delivered complex engineering programmes through others, managing priorities, resources, dependencies and technical risk.

You have practical experience developing and integrating embedded or robotics software in a physical product.

You can guide architectural decisions and review designs for software that interacts with hardware, balancing immediate delivery with maintainability and reuse.

You understand the challenges of bringing up new hardware and software platforms, including testing, fault diagnosis, validation and operational handover.

You build strong ownership of reliability and quality, using metrics and lessons from real-world operation to drive improvements.

You communicate clearly and can align teams with different priorities around shared technical outcomes.

Experience with automotive systems, drive-by-wire, CAN or automotive Ethernet, vehicle controls, or bench and hardware-in-the-loop testing is desirable.

 

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

  • Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)

  • Competency Interviews (Programming and hiring manager interview; 2 hours total)

  • Deep-dive technical interviews (programming, systems & domain-specific interviews; 3 hours total)

  • Final interview: Wayve value alignment (45 mins)

 

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

   

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

Nous aidons les entrepreneurs à se débarrasser des tâches chronophages liées à la comptabilité et à la finance, tout en leur donnant accès à des informations financières clés pour les aider à prendre les meilleures décisions pour leur entreprise.

Parallèlement, nous aidons les cabinets d'expertise-comptable, en leur permettant de passer moins de temps sur des tâches redondantes et répétitives, et plus de temps sur la partie conseil et accompagnement de leurs clients.

À propos de Pennylane

Pennylane est une des FinTech à la plus forte croissance en France, et souhaite bientôt adresser le marché européen.

En 6 ans d'existence, nous sommes parvenus à :

💻 Nous positionner sur le marché comme un éditeur de solution de comptabilité et de gestion financière innovant

💰 Lever un total de 400 millions d'euros, auprès d'investisseurs de renom, dont Sequoïa, le fonds phare de la Silicon Valley, connu pour avoir soutenu Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal et bien d'autres à leur début

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Passer de 7 cofondateurs à une équipe de 1000 collaborateurs, avec une note moyenne de 4,9/5 sur Glassdoor et 94% des évaluateurs Glassdoor qui recommanderaient PL à leurs proches!

🌍 Construire une équipe internationale composée de collaborateurs issus de 25 pays différents, avec une culture du télétravail très flexible

🤝 Gagner la confiance de milliers d'utilisateurs et obtenir d'excellents retours

🚀 Déjà plus de 1 million de TPE/PME et plus de 7 000 cabinets d’expertise-comptable utilisent Pennylane en France !

Tu as une solide expérience en comptabilité et tu aimes comprendre comment fonctionnent les outils SaaS ?
Tu souhaites intervenir sur des problématiques complexes, à la frontière entre métier, produit et technologie ?
Rejoins Pennylane en tant qu’Expert·e Support Technique et Comptable.

Ton rôle
Tu prends en charge les sujets les plus complexes remontés par nos utilisateurs et nos équipes Support.
Ton objectif : comprendre l’origine des problèmes, qu’ils soient comptables, fonctionnels ou techniques, puis coordonner leur résolution avec les équipes Produit et Tech.
Tu joueras un rôle clé entre les utilisateurs, le Support, les développeurs et les équipes Produit.

Tes missions

  • Investiguer des bugs, anomalies et problématiques comptables ou fonctionnelles.

  • Reproduire les problèmes rencontrés et en identifier la cause.

  • Qualifier les incidents et coordonner leur résolution avec les équipes concernées.

  • Échanger avec les développeurs et le Produit pour transmettre des analyses claires et exploitables.

  • Utiliser les outils d’investigation disponibles : logs et SQL simple.

  • Documenter les solutions et contribuer à l’amélioration continue du produit et des process.

  • Partager ton expertise avec les équipes Support.


Le profil recherché

Tu peux venir de différents environnements : cabinet d’expertise comptable ou éditeur de logiciel comptable.

Nous recherchons une personne qui :

  • dispose d’une solide expérience en comptabilité et comprend les problématiques des cabinets et entreprises ;

  • a déjà travaillé sur des sujets complexes nécessitant analyse et coordination ;

  • est à l’aise avec les outils et problématiques techniques ;

  • sait communiquer clairement avec des interlocuteurs métiers et techniques ;

  • parle anglais dans un contexte professionnel, à l’écrit comme à l’oral ;

  • fait preuve de rigueur, d’autonomie et de curiosité.

La connaissance de SQL est un plus, mais n’est pas indispensable. Ce qui compte surtout, c’est ton envie de comprendre les systèmes et de monter en compétence sur les sujets techniques.

Pourquoi rejoindre Pennylane ?

Tu rejoindras une équipe au cœur de la qualité produit, en lien direct avec les utilisateurs, les développeurs et les équipes Produit. Tu travailleras dans un environnement international, en forte croissance, où ton expertise comptable aura un impact concret

Process de recrutement :

  • Premier échange un/e recruteur - 30 min

  • Étude de cas et debriefing avec deux membres de l’équipe - 60 min

  • Entretien avec le Manager direct - Thibault et Viviane (Associate Team Lead Technical Support) - 60 min

  • Entretien avec Thomas (Team Lead Technical Support) - 45 min

🎁 Ce que l’on peut t'offrir :

🏥 Une mutuelle parmi les meilleures sur le marché (Alan Blue et Alan Mind)

🍜 Des tickets restaurants (Carte Swile)

🏝 Entre 6 et 12 jours de RTT supplémentaires aux 5 semaines de congés payés

🇬🇧 La possibilité de perfectionner ton anglais grâce à Busuu

🧑‍💻 Un budget dédié chaque mois pour tous nos Pennylaners, favorisant le travail depuis la maison ou en espace de coworking

🏢 Une facilité d’accès à nos bureaux, situés à quelques minutes de Saint Lazare en plein cœur de Paris

💵 Une enveloppe de BSPCE

🏃‍♀️ Un accès à 8000 salles de sport partout en France et plus de 300 activités de bien-être via notre partenaire Gymlib

💻 Un Mac

🎉 Nous pratiquons de nombreux sports ensemble et avons à cœur de nous réunir régulièrement autour d’événements d’entreprise tels que les Tech Days (qui permettent aux Pennylaners en remote de se réunir tous les 3 mois) ou notre séminaire d’entreprise qui a lieu une fois par an, et qui favorise de grands moments de cohésion pour toutes et tous.

Pour t'épanouir chez Pennylane, il faudra:

  • Parler anglais (le niveau est évalué et apprécié en fonction du département auquel tu postules)

  • Apprécier travailler dans un environnement en changement constant

  • Faire de la collaboration une priorité au sein de son équipe ou avec d'autres parties prenantes

  • Avoir un recul suffisant pour prioriser les actions à fort impact business dans son activité quotidienne.

Nous savons que certaines personnes sont moins susceptibles de postuler que d'autres si elles estiment ne pas remplir l'intégralité des critères.

Si tu hésites, nous t'encourageons à postuler quand même : qui sait, cela pourrait être le début d'une collaboration significative et durable !

Information importante à destination des candidat(e)s

Les tentatives d’arnaque au recrutement sont en hausse. Nous vous invitons à rester vigilant(e) lors de vos échanges.

Candidature uniquement via nos canaux officiels : postulez exclusivement via nos offres publiées sur nos supports officiels (site carrière, pages officielles partenaires).

Vérifiez systématiquement l’adresse e-mail de l’expéditeur : nos communications sont envoyées depuis des adresses professionnelles avec les domaine @pennylane.com ou @pennylane-partners.com .

Nous ne vous demanderons jamais de paiement, ni d’informations financières (coordonnées bancaires, paiement pour un entretien, achat de matériel, etc.) dans le cadre du recrutement.

Si une telle demande vous est faite, il s’agit d’une fraude. Nous vous invitons à ne pas répondre et à nous le signaler immédiatement."

Encourageant la diversité, équité et inclusion sous toutes ses formes, Pennylane offre un environnement de travail inclusif, bienveillant et propice à l’épanouissement, dans nos bureaux et en remote. Nous nous engageons à fournir les mêmes chances à tous nos candidats, indépendamment de leurs origines sociales et ethniques, genres, religions, orientations sexuelles ou handicaps.

🇫🇷 Données personnelles

Pennylane traite vos données pour gérer votre candidature et évaluer votre adéquation au poste. Si votre candidature n’aboutit pas, vos données peuvent être conservées 2 ans à compter de notre dernier échange ou de la clôture du recrutement afin de constituer & gérer un vivier de candidats. Vous pouvez vous opposer à tout moment et demander la suppression de vos données en écrivant à :
Notre data policy

🇬🇧 Personal Data

Pennylane processes your data to manage your application and assess your suitability for the position. If your application is unsuccessful, your data may be retained for 2 years from our last exchange or the closing of the recruitment process, in order to build and manage a candidate pool. You may object at any time and request the deletion of your data by writing to Learn more

🇩🇪 Personenbezogene Daten

Pennylane verarbeitet Ihre Daten, um Ihre Bewerbung zu bearbeiten und Ihre Eignung für die Stelle zu beurteilen. Sollte Ihre Bewerbung nicht erfolgreich sein, können Ihre Daten bis zu 2 Jahre ab unserem letzten Austausch oder dem Abschluss des Rekrutierungsverfahrens gespeichert werden, um einen Kandidatenpool aufzubauen und zu verwalten. Sie können jederzeit Widerspruch einlegen und die Löschung Ihrer Daten beantragen, indem Sie an Mehr erfahren

🇪🇸 Datos personales

Pennylane trata sus datos para gestionar su candidatura y evaluar su idoneidad para el puesto. En caso de que su candidatura no sea seleccionada, sus datos podrán conservarse hasta 2 años a partir de nuestro último contacto o de la finalización del proceso de selección, con el fin de constituir y gestionar una reserva de candidatos. Puede oponerse en cualquier momento y solicitar la eliminación de sus datos escribiendo a Más información

title: Founders Associate – Operations (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Über Vestlane und die Rolle

Vestlane ist die Plattform für Onboarding, KYC/AML und Tax Compliance für Private-Market-Fonds. Fondsmanager und Fondsadministratoren in ganz Europa wickeln über Vestlane ihre KYC-, AML- und Zeichnungsprozesse ab, in über 14 Jurisdiktionen und über den gesamten Investor-Lifecycle hinweg. Wir sind zertifiziert und für die regulatorische Realität spannender Akronyme gebaut – von GwG, BaFin, AMLR, RTS, CSSF bis hin zu DORA, RAIF, AIFMD, MiFID uvm.

Du willst sehen, wie ein B2B-SaaS-Unternehmen wirklich funktioniert – nicht aus der Folie, sondern aus dem Maschinenraum? Du willst die Welt von Venture Capital und Private Equity von innen kennenlernen, ohne den Umweg über drei Jahre Investment Banking? Du baust lieber einen Prozess, der ein Problem dauerhaft löst, als es jede Woche neu zu lösen? Du arbeitest mit KI-Tools und Automatisierung so selbstverständlich wie andere mit Excel? Dann ist diese Rolle für dich!

Als Founders Associate arbeitest du direkt mit unserem COO zusammen, der Operations und Go-to-Market verantwortet. Du übernimmst die operativen Themen, die heute auf seinem Tisch liegen – von Prozessen und Tooling über Finance und Compliance bis HR – und bist nah dran an jeder Entscheidung, die das Unternehmen bewegt. Echte Verantwortung ab Tag eins, direkter Draht zu Steuerberatung, Dienstleistern und Partnern, und ein Überblick über ein wachsendes SaaS-Unternehmen, den dir kein Konzern bietet. 2–3 Tage pro Woche arbeitet ihr gemeinsam vor Ort im Raum Erfurt/Weimar, an einem Arbeitsplatz, den du von Anfang an mit aufbaust; den Rest flexibel aus dem Home-Office.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Die interne Maschine bauen (dein Schwerpunkt): Du dokumentierst, standardisierst und automatisierst unsere internen Abläufe – von einem Wiki, das tatsächlich gelesen wird, über KI-Agenten für wiederkehrende Aufgaben bis zur Verwaltung unserer Tool- und Vendorlandschaft (Verträge, Zugänge, Kosten). Du erkennst, wo wir Zeit verlieren, und beseitigst die Ursache.

  • Entscheidungen vorbereiten: Du baust Analysen und Entscheidungsvorlagen für COO und CEO – Unit Economics, Markt- und Wettbewerbsrecherchen, Investorenreporting – und lieferst Zahlen statt Meinungen.

  • Finance und Accounting unterstützen: Du übernimmst die vorbereitende Buchhaltung, prüfst und stellst Rechnungen, bereitest Zahlungsläufe vor, arbeitest unserer Steuerberatung zu und hältst Kosten- und Liquiditätsübersichten aktuell.

  • Compliance-Operations am Laufen halten: Du pflegst Nachweise und Richtlinien für ISO 27001 und SOC 2, bereitest Audits vor und hältst unsere Subprozessorenliste und Fristen in Ordnung.

  • Hiring und HR mittragen: Du schreibst Stellenanzeigen, screenst Bewerbungen, koordinierst Interviews und sorgst dafür, dass neue Kolleg:innen sauber onboarded werden – von Arbeitsvertrag und Equipment bis zum ersten Tag. Daneben hältst du unsere HR-Prozesse und -Tools in Ordnung.

  • Verträge und Angebote im Griff behalten: Du bereitest Angebote vor, hältst unsere Pipeline in Salesforce aktuell und behältst Kunden-, Partner- und Auftragsverarbeitungsverträge im Blick – Versionen, Fristen, Unterschriften.

Dein Profil

  • Abgeschlossenes Studium (z. B. BWL, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Wirtschaftsrecht oder vergleichbar) oder eine abgeschlossene kaufmännische Ausbildung. Ob frisch von der Uni oder mit ein bis zwei Jahren Erfahrung aus Startup, Beratung oder Finanzbranche: Praktika und Werkstudententätigkeiten zählen, Haltung zählt mehr.

  • Sehr sicher in Excel/Google Sheets, strukturiert in Dokumentation und Projektmanagement. Erfahrung mit Salesforce, Buchhaltungs- oder Automatisierungstools (z. B. Zapier, Make, n8n) ist ein Plus.

  • Du arbeitest mit KI-Tools (Claude, ChatGPT o. ä.) nicht nur zum Texten, sondern um Prozesse zu bauen – und du weißt, wo du selbst prüfen musst.

  • Fließendes Deutsch und gutes Englisch – Partner, Dienstleister und Teile des Teams arbeiten auf Englisch.

  • Präzision und Pragmatismus: Du arbeitest selbstständig, fragst nach, wenn etwas unklar ist, und weißt, wann es auf jedes Detail ankommt – und wann nicht.

  • Du hast kein Problem damit, morgens eine Rechnung zu prüfen und nachmittags ein Bewerbungsgespräch zu organisieren. Breite ist für dich kein Mangel an Fokus, sondern die Chance, das ganze Unternehmen zu verstehen und zu Lernen.

  • Interesse an Fonds, Finanzregulierung oder Compliance ist willkommen, Vorwissen keine Voraussetzung – das bringen wir dir bei.

  • Du siehst dich als Unternehmer:in innerhalb von Vestlane, nicht als Zuarbeiter:in. Du willst heute Verantwortung und morgen Führung, und du willst dir beides erarbeiten, indem du etwas aufbaust.

title: Founding implementation strategist [ERP + AI]
descriptionHtml:
TL;DR

  • We're building the SAP/NetSuite of the AI era for mid-sized companies in the real-world economy, starting with their supply chain operations (buy, sell, stock, produce)

  • Founding deployment strategist: you deploy two things into real factories, in the same project, the ERP that runs their operations, and the AI agents that work inside it. Every client goes from signed contract to go-live on the date we promised, running on Piston, with agents already doing part of the work

  • A rare shape: someone who has led client projects that landed in industrial companies, who is genuinely AI-native, and who will write the deployment playbook for the team and our system integrator partners

  • €3M Pre-seed (Top-tier VCs)

What this role is (and isn't)

Most ERP deployments are people moving data around for a year. Incumbents quote six figures for it, and the client gets the same software they had, just newer. Ours run in eight to twelve weeks and deliver two things at once: a new ERP that runs buying, selling, stock and production, and AI agents inside it that read the orders, recompute the production load, prepare the purchases, and ask a human only when it matters.

This is not a product or a sales role, you are a deployment strategist. In one project, you replace a company's ERP and you put AI agents to work inside it.

Why now

Since day one, the founders have run every deployment themselves. Clients are now coming in faster than we can handle, and we need someone to own deployments. You work directly with Eric, CEO, who also leads product. That puts you as close as it gets to what success means at Piston: the success of our clients.

What you'll do

  • Deploy the ERP, with AI. The client's sales, purchasing, stock and production move onto Piston: data migrated from their old ERP and their Excel files, configuration built from their own documents, training, go-live. AI does the heavy lifting, you do the judgment.

  • Put the first AI agents live, during the ERP deployment. You decide what each agent does on its own, what it hands to a human for approval, and you make sure it's still running three months later.

  • Write the deployment playbook. Every go-live feeds a playbook that our next deployment hires and our system integrator partners will follow.

  • Map where the client's time goes. On site, you find the work that eats people's days: re-keying orders, chasing suppliers, rebuilding the same Excel every month. That map is the backlog of the next agents.

  • Teach humans to work with agents. The people you deploy with have never supervised software that acts on its own. You show them how to trust it, check it and correct it.

  • Hold the date and the budget. You size each deployment before the contract and protect that budget.

  • Use the tools engineers build for you. Our engineers build the tools that let you deploy on your own: AI-assisted data migration from the client's old ERP and Excel files, and a builder for screens and agents. You tell them what slows you down, they make it disappear.

  • Agentify your own work. On top of the tools our engineers build, you create your own agents for the deployment itself: configuration checks, test scenarios, training material, status reports. Every manual step you repeat twice becomes an agent for the next deployment.

What you bring

You bring the energy to deploy AI at scale in industrial companies. You learn fast from discovery, and you're as comfortable with founders and leadership teams as with operators on the shop floor.

Must have

  • Customer-facing project experience. Two years or more managing client projects in an industrial environment, typically in consulting (operations, supply chain, transformation). You've held deadlines, managed stakeholders, and delivered.

  • AI-native, for real. You use LLMs every day, and you've built things with them: automations, agents, prompts that run in production (Claude, GPT, n8n, Make, scripts, whatever works). You know what an agent can do alone, where it breaks, and where a human must stay in the loop.

  • Listening before configuring. You translate what people say into what the system and the agents must do, and you notice when the two don't match.

  • At ease in front of clients: Plant directors, finance, shop-floor operators. You can hold a room, and say no in it.

  • A full load, gladly. Around 150 project days a year, several deployments running at once.

  • Fluent English and French, both required. Our first clients work in French, our team writes in English, and you may support our deployments in the United States.

Nice to have

  • You've automated a real operations process end to end, with measurable hours saved

  • You've already taken a complex B2B software live

  • Comfortable with AI

  • You've worked around manufacturing or food operations: lots, BOMs, production orders, campaigns

  • Seed / Series A experience, where nobody's job description holds for long

Talent beats checklists. If you're intrigued, apply anyway.

How we'll measure success

  • ERP go-lives on the date we promised

  • Days spent against the plan we sold

  • Agents still running three months after launch, and the hours of work they take off the client's hands

What you'll get

  • World-class peers

  • The first hire of our deployment team: you write the playbook that future hires and our system integrator partners will follow, and you grow with the team it builds

  • A front-row seat on how AI agents change the way real companies operate

  • Regular company offsite (2–4 times per year) in great locations

  • Ideal equipment and setup

  • Remote-first (France), about 20% of your time on client sites

Process

We value efficiency and clarity. The entire process takes no more than 2 weeks:

  1. 30-minute intro call with Florian (CRO)

  2. 60-minute deployment deep dive with Eric (CEO)

  3. 30-min cultural-fit interview with Eugène (CTO)

  4. 2 days paid assessment, on a real client situation.

  5. Offer: If it's a match, we move fast.

Interested? Tell us about a client project you led, and something you automated with AI. A short, personal note goes a long way, AI-generated cover letters don't.

title: Founding Operations & Systems Lead
descriptionHtml:
Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.
We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.

Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms, allowing you to run everything from your phone - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legal structuring and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.

We're already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $750m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.

 

Why we're hiring

  • We are automating a decades old part of the financial services industry. AI pilled builders like you are the beating heart of this plan, because LLMs & agents allow us to turn this services business entirely into software.

  • This is a product role, and your product is how Odin operates. Think of it as our ghostbuster: every operational problem lands with you, you decide what gets fixed, and you ship most of the fixes yourself rather than writing tickets for someone else.

  • We're post-PMF, fast-growing, and rolling out new products (fund admin) & geographies (USA). Customer & deal volume is climbing fast.

  • Today we're on track for roughly 700 deals a year, with a team of ~20, and we'll process $500m-$750m of investment in 2026 alone.

  • The next goal is 7,000 deals a year and billions in annual investment flows.

  • We believe this can be achieved with a team of around 50 people. But it will only be possible if we turn human-driven services workflows into software.

  • Odin's operations run on around 50 processes, some code and some people, and plenty still held together by spreadsheets. Your job is to take each one apart, question why it exists, then rebuild it or kill it.

  • The simplest way to think about it: the numerator is how many deals we close, the denominator is what each deal costs us to run. You'll focus on the denominator, and the right person won't be able to stop themselves thinking about the numerator too.

  • We expect the right hire to be spending more time in Claude Code than in Excel, email or anything else.

     

What you'll own

  • Triage: Every operational problem comes to you before it reaches product and engineering. For each one you decide: scope it so precisely that engineering knows exactly what to build, or build it yourself.

  • Cost per deal: There will be big early wins where a whole process can be ripped out and replaced. After that, doubling ops efficiency comes from 150 small changes, and you'll be the one making them.

  • Automation: You'll sit with the deal operations team, learn each workflow end to end, then build what replaces it. Most of what you ship you'll build without engineering. What does go to them arrives simple, scoped and usually with a working prototype attached.

  • Deleting things and saying no: You decide what belongs in our processes and what doesn't. If a request from sales doesn't scale and isn't highly profitable we don't do it. If a way of working exists for no good reason, you kill it.

  • The ops team: You'll lead the core deal operations team, deciding where their time goes while you rebuild the work around them.

     

What we're looking for

  • You build, not buy: Clear evidence, at work or in your own time, that you've built real solutions with AI with no budget and no engineers. Buying a tool or setting up workflows in Sheets doesn't count. We want to see what you've shipped in Claude Code or similar.

  • Founder or product DNA: You've founded something, been early on a founding team, or worked as a product manager. That usually means four or more years of experience and a track record of finishing what you start.

  • Systems thinker: You look at any process the way a good product manager looks at a product: What's the job? Why are we doing this at all? What's the smallest, simplest system that achieves the goal? You think about the whole business, not just your corner of it.
    A lot of what happens in fund admin is inherited convention, an industry "given", or a constraint of some third party. You should find it physically difficult to accept any of that.

  • In the details and extremely on top of things: You understand every single aspect of our systems end to end. You close loops, you chase, you push hard to get things done.

  • Numerate: Comfortable with financial mechanics, strong mental arithmetic. You'll be automating a lot of numerical work - carry, allocations, fee calculations, distributions, and the edge cases that make all of them interesting.

  • Big plus: regulated financial services background: Fund administration, custody, payments, brokerage, audit, tax or another back office function. Useful, but not required. We care much more about the traits you have and the things you can build than specific skills or experience on your CV.

     

How we work

There are five things we care about deeply:

  1. Reason from the ground up
    Seek to understand what is true by always asking why. Do not trust convention or experts.

  2. Speed begets speed
    We work fast. Speed compounds, it's the best form of defensibility, and it's energising to be around. If you work slowly, or tolerate slow work around you, you do not belong at Odin.

  3. Take ownership
    Do not wait for permission to do things. Find the answer, force the thing into existence and hold others to an extremely high standard - the same standard you hold yourself to.

  4. Brutal honesty
    If work doesn't meet the bar, people need to hear it, and the right people want to.

  5. Truly excellent customer service
    Be a stickler for detail in every single interaction a customer has with us, and always strive to make this experience better, smoother, faster.

     

This role is probably not for you if

  • You'd rather write specs and hand tickets to engineers than build the thing yourself;

  • You prefer close management of your responsibilities;

  • You are risk-averse;

  • You want a 9-5;

  • You take yourself too seriously;

  • You care about working for a company that's raised lots of money rather than one that's extremely capital efficient and focused on building a profitable giant that has a positive economic impact

     

Salary

£90k - £120k base, plus a meaningful equity grant. We're flexible on the mix of cash and equity.

 

Hiring process

Three stages, usually inside two weeks, with detailed feedback within 24 hours of each one. A call with our Head of People, an in-person session with the founders where you solve a real Odin problem end to end with AI, then a final with the founders. The last two can run on the same day.

 

Location & ways of working

We're a London-based team. This role works closely with the founders, product and the wider ops team, and the speed we run at makes that much easier in-person. At least three days a week in the office.

 

Benefits

  • Health: Private health insurance (Vitality), paid sick leave including support for pregnancy loss and fertility treatments, and access to Spill for mental health support

  • Wellness: £1,000 annual budget for health, therapy or fitness

  • Parental Leave: Enhanced maternity, adoption, paternity and partner leave

  • Pension: 4% employer contribution with salary sacrifice options

  • Time Off: 25 days annual leave, 2 wellness days and flexible bank holidays (33 days total)

  • Work From Anywhere: Up to 6 weeks per year working from anywhere globally

  • Birthday Leave: An additional day of leave

title: FPGA Engineer - Electronic Warfare
descriptionHtml:
About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role

As an FPGA Engineer within our Electronic Warfare team, you will design and implement the real-time digital signal processing that turns raw RF into actionable effect — from receiver channelization and threat detection through to jamming waveform generation. You will own the RTL at the heart of our EW and SIGINT systems, working hand-in-hand with the RF hardware, embedded software and algorithm teams to take a signal chain from concept and simulation to silicon, to the lab, and into the field.

Responsibilities

  • RTL Design & Implementation: Design and implement signal-processing datapaths in VHDL or SystemVerilog — digital down-conversion, channelizers, filtering, FFT and detection chains — from specification through to validation.

  • Real-Time DSP in Fabric: Implement detection, direction-finding, classification and waveform generation under hard latency and throughput budgets, translating algorithm intent into fixed-point hardware.

  • RF & Data Converter Interfacing: Own the digital interface to the RF front-end — high-speed converters (JESD204B/C), multi-channel clocking, synchronization and calibration paths.

  • Hardware/Software Partitioning: Define the split between programmable logic and on-chip processors, and the register and streaming interfaces the embedded software team builds against.

  • Timing Closure & Resource Budgets: Drive constraints, timing closure, and resource, power and thermal budgets on production hardware.

  • Bring-up, Integration & Validation: Lead FPGA bring-up on new boards, bench validation against performance targets with RF instrumentation, and over-the-air testing alongside the systems team.

  • Technical Coordination: Collaborate across RF hardware, embedded, GNC and ML teams on system integration and technical interfaces.

  • System Reviews & Documentation: Contribute to design and architecture reviews, maintaining consistency between requirements, design and testing.

Candidate Requirements

  • Strong RTL design background in VHDL or SystemVerilog for signal-processing datapaths is mandatory.

  • Solid digital signal processing fundamentals: sampling, mixing, decimation, filter design, FFT, and fixed-point arithmetic and quantization trade-offs.

  • Hands-on experience with SoC FPGAs and their toolchains..

  • No prior Electronic Warfare experience required.

  • Experience with high-speed data converter interfaces (JESD204B/C) and multi-channel synchronization is a definite plus.

  • Experience with algorithm-to-RTL workflows (MATLAB/Simulink, Python modelling, or HLS) is a plus.

  • Lab experience with RF instrumentation — spectrum analyzer, vector signal generator, oscilloscope — is a plus.

  • MSc in Electrical / Electronics Engineering, Signal Processing or a related field;

  • Broad engineering culture with understanding of RF hardware, embedded software and system-level trade-offs.

  • Rigorous, structured and mission-driven mindset with strong analytical skills.

  • Excellent communication and documentation abilities.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

Warum roadsurfer?

TEAMSPIRIT & TEAMEVENTS: Freu dich auf eine kollegiale Atmosphäre mit flachen Hierarchien, jede Menge Spaß und großartigem Teamspirit sowie regelmäßige Teamevents wie gemeinsame Sportsessions, Grillabende oder einfach nur ein Feierabenddrink an deiner Station.

CAMPER BUDGET: Du bekommst eine jährliche Freimiete für unsere Camper, damit du den #happyroadsurfing Lifestyle selbst erleben kannst.

DISCOUNTS UND BENEFITS: Nutze unsere Corporate Benefits Plattform, die Travel Industry Card und Family & Friends Rabatte.

DEVELOPMENT & GROWTH: Wachstum spielt eine zentrale Rolle bei roadsurfer! Bei unseren regelmäßigen Station Life Camps und Trainings kannst du dich mit Teammitgliedern aus aller Welt vernetzen und deine Fähigkeiten verbessern – sei es im Bereich Fahrzeugwissen oder Kundenservice – stets begleitet von unseren Learning & Training-Expert:innen.

BUDDY PROGRAMM: Zum Start begleitet dich eine erfahrene Person aus einer anderen Station – in der gleichen Position, aber an einem anderen Standort. So hast du direkt eine feste Ansprechperson und lernst den roadsurfer Spirit über deine eigene Station hinaus kennen.

Deine Rolle – Deine Leidenschaft

  • Du koordinierst das tägliche Vermietgeschäft und sorgst gemeinsam mit unserem Stationsteam für einen reibungslosen Ablauf bei Fahrzeugübergaben und -rücknahmen.

  • Die Zufriedenheit unserer Kund*innen steht für dich im Mittelpunkt – du gestaltest eine positive Customer Journey.

  • Du unterstützt die Stationsleitung bei der Personalplanung sowie beim Training des Teams und trägst dazu bei, dass sich alle weiterentwickeln können.

  • Du stellst sicher, dass unsere Qualitätsstandards eingehalten werden – insbesondere im Umgang mit unseren Kund*innen

Was du brauchst, um mit uns auf einer Welle zu surfen

  • Eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung und 2–3 Jahre Berufserfahrung, idealerweise in der Autovermietung, im Tourismus oder in einem vergleichbaren Bereich.

  • Hohe Service- und Kundenorientierung sowie ein freundliches, professionelles und offenes Auftreten.

  • Freude daran, aktiv mit anzupacken, sowie Kommunikationsstärke im direkten Kontakt mit unseren Kund*innen.

  • Organisationstalent und die Fähigkeit, auch in herausfordernden Situationen den Überblick zu behalten und Lösungen zu finden.

  • Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift.

  • Einen gültigen Führerschein der Klasse B.

Dein Gehalt

Wir ❤️ Transparenz. Das Gehaltsband für diese Position liegt zwischen 34.000 EUR und 38.000 EUR brutto jährlich. Wir führen aktuell Gehaltsbänder in unseren Stellenbeschreibungen ein, um sicherzustellen, dass alle Mitarbeitenden fair behandelt werden. Sobald wir uns im Bewerbungsprozess besser kennenlernen und deine Fähigkeiten und Erfahrungen noch genauer einschätzen können, finden wir gemeinsam heraus, welche Stufe innerhalb des Gehaltsbands am besten zu dir passt. In einem jährlichen Feedbackgespräch wird dein Gehalt mindestens einmal im Jahr überprüft.

Bereit zu surfen?

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung! Für Rückfragen kannst du dich auch gern jederzeit an ----- wenden. Bitte bewirb dich ausschließlich über unser Bewerbertool – so geht nichts verloren und wir können deine Bewerbung schnell bearbeiten.

ABOUT #ROADSURFER

We are more than Europe's largest campervan rental company. In 2021 we launched our platform roadsurfer spots in addition to our other products rent, abo and sales – a platform where you can discover and book unique camping spots. But that’s only the beginning. We are growing fast, so hop on board and join us on our journey. The roadsurfer philosophy is simple: rent an RV, start your adventure, be happy. Come ride the wave with us!
